description:
Found by defk-8i4 (branch defk-8i4/levenshtein-cutoff, examples/fuzzy_search/bench/elixir_variants.exs): a Myers bit-parallel Levenshtein in plain Elixir runs ~18-19 ms/query vs ~60 ms for the shipped DP+cutoff Elixir backend and ~14 ms for the defk kernel (provisional, busy machine). That would make fuzzy_search 'marginal' rather than 'good'. Per AGENTS.md, give both sides the same algorithm: implement Myers in the defk kernel (needs bitwise operators, defk-w38; words longer than 64 chars need the multi-word variant or a fallback) and make Myers the optimized Elixir baseline (baseline: :optimized). Also try the length pre-filter / tighter bound on both sides.

Done when both backends use Myers with identical results (fuzzy_search tests), the variants table and README verdict are updated, and numbers are flagged provisional until the defk-klw quiet-machine run.

comments.text: Done in ea52871 (merge 346a0c3). Both backends: Myers for 1..62-byte queries, DP otherwise; cut-off on |n-m| and score-(n-i); branch-free score step on both sides. Provisional (load 4-7): Elixir 60 -> 10.9-11.1 ms/query, defk 13.7 -> 4.6-4.7, blocking 3.9; defk vs Elixir 4.4x -> 2.3-2.4x (still good, not marginal: Myers in the kernel gained 3x too). Under load: Elixir 698-741 req/s, defk 1791-1839, blocking 2264-2367; blocking /health p99 75-82 -> 18-20 ms. Yield cost +19% from a per-word safepoint -> defk-w8r.1. Tried, no gain in the kernel: wrap64 on the checked add; branch-free score (kept for symmetry). Elixir variants 11-14 in bench/elixir_variants.exs. Docs: fuzzy_search README, examples/README row + paragraph, README row, performance.md 1.6, 2.7, 6.4. Quiet-machine re-measure still due.
Reopened 2026-10-15: code moved from a local merge into PR #1 (https://github.com/DanielLuning/defk/pull/1) under the new PR workflow (defk-ecs). Close after the owner merges it.

title: Myers bit-parallel Levenshtein in both fuzzy_search backends
